lessons.title: Story Time: The Leaves Are Falling
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss seasonal changes described in a story.
success_criteria: I can say what changed in the story.
I can name an autumn feature.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read an autumn-themed story, modelling discussion of seasonal change.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer questions about the seasonal changes in the story.
key_questions: What sign of autumn is this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of seasonal change — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap signs of autumn in the story.
lessons.home_link: Look for a sign of autumn outside.

lessons.title: Measuring Leaves: Length in Centimetres
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure length in centimetres using a ruler.
success_criteria: I can measure using a ruler.
I can record the length in centimetres.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap measuring with cubes from Year 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model measuring leaves using a ruler, reading centimetre measurements.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure a collection of leaves using a ruler, recording lengths in cm.
key_questions: How many centimetres long is this leaf?

differentiation.greater_depth: Measure 5+ leaves and order by length

lessons.assessment_notes: Record standard unit measuring skill, building on Year 1's introduction — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Measure a leaf or object at home with a ruler.

lessons.title: Suitable Materials for Autumn Clothing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify suitable materials for autumn weather.
success_criteria: I can name a material suitable for autumn.
I can say why it's suitable.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what to wear in autumn weather.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss material properties suitable for autumn (waterproof, warm) recapping Year 1 material learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort clothing items by material suitability for autumn weather, recording reasoning.
key_questions: Is this material suitable for rain?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note recap and application of material suitability — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Check what material your coat or raincoat is made from.

lessons.title: Writing About Autumn
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write descriptive sentences about autumn using expanded noun phrases.
success_criteria: I can use an expanded noun phrase.
I can write a sentence about autumn.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap expanded noun phrases from Week 2.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a descriptive sentence about autumn using an expanded noun phrase (e.g. 'the crisp, golden leaves').
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 descriptive sentences about autumn.
key_questions: Can you use an expanded noun phrase?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ sentences with varied noun phrases

lessons.assessment_notes: Note grammar application in descriptive writing — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share autumn sentences with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe autumn to your family using an expanded noun phrase.

lessons.title: Autumn Data: Leaf Colour Survey
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to conduct and represent a survey about leaf colours.
success_criteria: I can conduct a survey.
I can represent the data in a chart.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap data handling from earlier weeks.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model conducting a survey of leaf colours found, representing data in a block diagram or pictogram.
lessons.independent_task: Children conduct a leaf colour survey and represent the data, answering questions about it.

differentiation.support: Adult supports survey and chart construction

lessons.assessment_notes: Record data handling consolidation applied to a science context — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap the leaf colour survey findings.
lessons.home_link: Collect and sort leaves by colour at home.

lessons.title: Squashing, Bending, Twisting, Stretching
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how materials can change shape.
success_criteria: I can name a way to change a material's shape.
I can test a material this way.
lessons.starter_activity: Try squashing, bending, twisting and stretching playdough.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the four ways materials can change shape (squash, bend, twist, stretch) with demonstrations.
lessons.independent_task: Children test different materials for each way of changing shape, recording results.
resources_needed: Range of test materials (paper, fabric, playdough, elastic)

differentiation.greater_depth: Test all 4 methods on multiple materials

lessons.assessment_notes: Note introduction of a key new Year 2 material science concept — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap the four ways materials can change shape.
lessons.home_link: Test squashing, bending, twisting or stretching safely at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Autumn Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read autumn-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read autumn words.
I can read a sentence about autumn.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to autumn-themed words (e.g. 'leaf', 'acorn', 'crisp').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading autumn words over the week.

lessons.title: Autumn Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using an autumn context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using an autumn context (e.g. conkers/acorns collected).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve autumn-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up an autumn word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Which Materials Change Shape Best?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare how easily different materials change shape.
success_criteria: I can compare materials for one shape-change method.
I can say which is easiest.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the four shape-change methods from Tuesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing how easily different materials can be squashed, bent, twisted or stretched.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare 3-4 materials for a chosen shape-change method, ranking by ease.
key_questions: Which material was easiest to bend?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative testing skill — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap materials ranked by ease of shape change.
lessons.home_link: Test how easily two materials change shape at home.

lessons.title: Autumn Nature Walk Discussion
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe observations from a nature walk clearly.
success_criteria: I can describe what I observed.
I can use autumn vocabulary.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap autumn vocabulary learned this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model describing observations using rich vocabulary.
lessons.independent_task: Children go on a short nature walk (or view photos) and describe their observations to a partner.
resources_needed: Access to outdoor space or nature photos
key_questions: What autumn word could describe it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and vocabulary application — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.home_link: Go on an autumn walk with your family.

lessons.title: Shapes in Nature: Autumn Leaves
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify shapes and symmetry in natural autumn objects.
success_criteria: I can identify a shape in a leaf.
I can say if it's symmetrical.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss shapes and symmetry found in autumn leaves and conkers.
lessons.independent_task: Children examine leaves/natural objects, recording shapes and symmetry observed.

differentiation.greater_depth: Identify multiple shapes and explain symmetry reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape/symmetry application to a natural science context — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Recap shapes and symmetry found in nature.
lessons.home_link: Look for shapes and symmetry in nature at home.

lessons.title: Designing with Changeable Materials
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use a material's changeable properties in a simple design.
success_criteria: I can choose a material for its changeable property.
I can use it in a simple design.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss choosing a material for a design based on its ability to change shape (e.g. a bendy bookmark, a stretchy hairband).
lessons.independent_task: Children create a simple design/model using a material's changeable property purposefully.
resources_needed: Range of materials (pipe cleaners, elastic, foil)
key_questions: Why did you choose this material?

differentiation.support: Adult supports material choice and construction

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of material property knowledge to a design task — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Share designs created using changeable materials.
lessons.home_link: Find something at home made from a bendy or stretchy material.

lessons.title: Autumn and Materials Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about autumn and materials.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about autumn and materials, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What happens to leaves in autumn?
Why might elastic be a good material for a hairband?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on this week's facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Measuring and Data Consolidation
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply measuring and data handling skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can measure in centimetres.
I can read a chart of survey data.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of measuring in cm and data handling.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: measuring, data handling.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 12 maths observations for each child, completing Autumn 2 — evidence for MATHS.MEA/STAT.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising measuring in centimetres over the break.

lessons.title: Autumn and Materials Topic Recap and Autumn Term Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about autumn changes and changeable materials.
success_criteria: I can name a sign of autumn.
I can name a way to change a material's shape.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole autumn term's science learning.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the term's learning across living things, habitats, and materials.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a final class display celebrating the whole Autumn term's science learning.
key_questions: What have we learned about autumn and materials?
What was your favourite science topic this term?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: End of Autumn term science consolidation summary for each child — evidence for SCI.MAT/SCI.LIV.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate a fantastic Autumn term of Year 2 science and learning overall.
lessons.home_link: Share your favourite thing you learned this term with your family.
